question: Which description matches a trill?

options.text: The written note, the note below, then the written note
options.explanation: That three-note figure is a lower mordent. A trill keeps alternating for the length of the note.

options.text: A rapid alternation of the written note and the note above
options.explanation: A trill, marked tr, alternates the printed note with the note a step above it, quickly, for the value of the note.

options.text: Note above, written note, note below, written note
options.explanation: Those four notes are a turn. A trill is a repeated alternation, not a single four-note shape.

options.text: A crushed grace note with a slash through its stem
options.explanation: A little note with a slash is an acciaccatura. It is played as quickly as possible, not as a sustained alternation.

explanation: A trill is the rapid alternation of the written note and the note above. At this grade you are asked to recognise it, including when the alternation has been written out.

question: The quick figure at the start of the bar (G–F–G) matches which ornament on G? Ignore the rest.
notationAlt: Treble staff, no sharps or flats. Three short notes fall G, F, G, then the bar is completed by a rest.

options.text: Upper mordent
options.explanation: An upper mordent on G would be G–A–G, using the note above. This figure goes down to F.

options.text: Lower mordent
options.explanation: A lower mordent is the written note, the note below, and the written note again. G–F–G is exactly that pattern on G.

options.text: Turn
options.explanation: A turn on G needs four notes: A–G–F–G. Only three notes are printed, and they start on G rather than on A.

options.text: Inverted turn
options.explanation: An inverted turn on G starts on the note below: F–G–A–G. The printed figure is G–F–G.

explanation: G–F–G is the written-out lower mordent on G: main note, lower neighbour, main note.

question: A turn on D is written out as:

options.text: E D C D
options.explanation: A turn plays the note above, the written note, the note below, and the written note again. On D that is E–D–C–D.

options.text: C D E D
options.explanation: C–D–E–D starts on the lower note. That is an inverted turn on D, not the ordinary turn.

options.text: D E D
options.explanation: D–E–D uses the upper neighbour only once. That is an upper mordent, which has three notes rather than four.

options.text: D C D
options.explanation: D–C–D is a lower mordent. A turn includes both the upper and the lower neighbour.

explanation: The ordinary turn on D is the upper note, the main note, the lower note, and the main note: E–D–C–D.

question: An appoggiatura before an undotted crotchet normally takes:

options.text: No time from the main note; it is crushed in as quickly as possible
options.explanation: That description fits the acciaccatura, the grace note with a slash through the stem. An appoggiatura is a leaning note and it does take time.

options.text: Half the value of the crotchet, leaving the main note as a quaver
options.explanation: Before a plain note, the appoggiatura takes half the value. Half of a crotchet is a quaver, and the main note keeps the other quaver.

options.text: The whole crotchet, so the main note is not played
options.explanation: The appoggiatura borrows time, but the main note is still played. It is not replaced entirely.

options.text: Two-thirds of the crotchet
options.explanation: Two-thirds is the rule when the main note is dotted. A plain crotchet is not dotted, so the appoggiatura takes half, not two-thirds.

explanation: An appoggiatura before an undotted note takes half that note's value. In front of a crotchet it is played as a quaver, and the crotchet is left as a quaver.

question: An acciaccatura is printed as:

options.text: A small note with a stroke through its stem
options.explanation: The slash through the stem is the sign of the acciaccatura. It is crushed in as quickly as possible, taking no real value from the main note.

options.text: The letters tr above the note
options.explanation: tr is the sign for a trill, a rapid alternation with the note above.

options.text: A sideways S-shaped sign above the note
options.explanation: That sign is a turn. It stands for four notes around the written note, not a single crushed grace note.

options.text: A small note with no stroke, taking half the value of the following note
options.explanation: A small note without a stroke, taking a share of the value, is an appoggiatura. The acciaccatura is the one with the stroke.

explanation: The acciaccatura is the grace note with a line through the stem, played as quickly as possible.
